plain_english: The supplied page is Andrew Glasgow's testament-testamentar and inventory. His residence is provisionally read as Corsoun in the parish of Caldercleir, sheriffdom of Edinburgh. It records his death on 7 February and says that he gave up the inventory himself on 6 February. The latter-will opening at the bottom expressly bears 6 February 1597 as written.

The inventory includes cows with calves, young cattle, horses, sheep, oats, barley, household furnishings and clothing. Incoming and outgoing accounts name financial associates, but their appearance here does not establish family relationships.

The latter will only begins at the foot of image 123. A local page-two continuation is now supplied, but its family appointments and distribution clauses remain outside this earlier fresh transcription. The previous review's wife, children and conditional unborn-child clauses therefore still await fresh verification.
findings: Image 123, lines 4-9: this is a testament-testamentar, distinct from a testament-dative. The decedent's own act on the sixth and death on the seventh are legible; uncertain year numerals in the opening should be checked against the clearer 1597 at the latter-will opening.

Image 123, line 42: 6 February 1597 is the written latter-will date. The existing record describes this as 1597/8 under the pre-1600 Scottish year convention; that is a dating interpretation, not a different date written on the image.
Image 123, lines 24-36: financial associates and possible Stevenson names are not described here as Andrew's parents, children or siblings.

The page header identifies image 123 and last image 124. The continuation is now present locally, but no wife/son/daughter clause occurs in the portion freshly reviewed. Coverage therefore remains partial until page two receives a fresh line-by-line reading.
